validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE: confirmed via 2+ independent RU-language sources describing a real, distinct third parallel pipe in the Gazli-Kagan corridor. uzreport.news (2002-01-16, 'Газли-Каган - новый газопровод в Узбекистане') and uz2002.ru (2002-04-05, 'ИТЕРА завершает строительство газопровода Газли-Каган') both independently describe a ~2001-2002 ITERA-financed 'магистральный газопровод' (trunk gas pipeline) Gazli-Kagan project, cost 'общей стоимостью 30 млн долларов США' targeted for completion 'к середине 2002 года'. Separately, Sputnik Uzbekistan (2021-11-29, on the launch of a 4th line) explicitly enumerates the corridor's history: lines 1 and 2 launched 1973-1983, and the THIRD line ('третья нитка') opened in 2006 -- directly corroborating this row as segment III, distinct from P2290 (segments I/II, ~1973-1983) and P3983 (segment IV, launched 2021-2022). This is genuine parallel pipe per an affirmative source describing each line separately (the Kazakhstan cluster-A standard), not a duplicate/double-count of P2290 or P3983. CLASSIFICATION correct: both 2002 sources explicitly call it a 'магистральный газопровод' (trunk/transmission gas pipeline), confirming PipelineType=transmission and Fuel=Gas. DATES: ConstructionYear=2002 and SegmentCost=$30,000,000 both match the 2002 sources exactly (construction/contract phase); StartYear1=2006 matches Sputnik's explicit 'third line opened 2006' (full operational completion, after further build-out on the km 0-10 and km 78-116 sections per search-engine snippets tracing to the sheet's own ngm.uz ref -- see Length caveat). CAVEAT ON LENGTH: LengthKnown=116.00 km already carries a ref (ngm.uz, http://ngm.uz/ru/page/view/22) but that page returned HTTP 503 on three separate live fetch attempts today, and its Wayback capture (20250905224526, confirmed to exist via the availability API) could not be read because web.archive.org content-serving was unreachable from this environment all of 2026-08-26 -- a known network condition, not evidence of deletion (per the country note precedent). I could not independently verify the 116 km figure. The 2002 sources describe the SAME cost ($30M) project as only 67 km, which is NOT 116 km -- search-engine snippets (sourced only to the same inaccessible ngm.uz page) suggest the discrepancy resolves as phased construction (a ~67-68 km 2002 phase plus a 48 km 2005-2006 phase across two sub-sections, km 0-10 and 78-116, summing to the full 116 km corridor), which would reconcile ConstructionYear=2002 and StartYear1=2006 as two real construction phases rather than a conflict -- but I cannot cite that reconciliation from an independent, currently-reachable source. RECOMMENDATION: re-check ngm.uz (or its Wayback capture) once reachable; if it reproduces the km-marker breakdown, Length is corroborated and the two-phase story should be documented in ResearcherNotes. Do not drop the existing ngm.uz ref -- 503 + an unreachable-today Wayback capture is not a confirmed deletion.

validity.recommendation: Re-examine Capacity=35.00 mill.Sm3/day on P3984 (and the identical value on sibling P2290) -- likely a corridor-total figure duplicated across two segment rows rather than each segment's own throughput.
validity.researcher_notes: The only sourced capacity figure I could find for the Gazli-Kagan corridor is from Sputnik Uzbekistan (2021-11-29): 'за сутки через данный магистральный газопровод проходит 35 млн кубометров природного газа' -- i.e. 35 million m3/day is the COMBINED throughput of the corridor's THREE THEN-EXISTING lines (I, II, III) as of just before the 4th line's addition (which was to add a further +25 million m3/day). That is a corridor-level aggregate, not segment III's individual capacity. Compounding this: the roster shows P2290 (segments I and II combined) ALSO carries Capacity=35.00 -- the identical figure on a different row. Two different rows (P2290 covering lines I+II, and P3984 covering line III alone) cannot both correctly carry the SAME 35 mmcm/day as their own individual capacity when the sourced fact is that 35 mmcm/day was the sum across all three lines combined. This has the signature of the corridor-total figure being copied onto both rows rather than split per segment. By contrast P3983 (segment IV) carries Capacity=25.00, which DOES match its own individually-sourced figure ('дополнительно 25 миллионов кубометров природного газа в сутки', i.e. that segment's own added capacity) -- so P3983's capacity looks correctly segment-specific while P2290's and P3984's do not. I did not find any source giving segment III's capacity on its own, so I cannot supply a corrected value -- flagging for Update rather than proposing a fabricated split.

fills.researcher_notes: Sputnik (2021-11-29) frames the third line as one of three already-operating lines (opened 2006) whose combined 35 mmcm/day throughput the 4th line is being added alongside -- confirms segment III is in active service as of Nov 2021, no indication of any outage since.
Both independent 2002 sources explicitly describe it as a 'газопровод' (gas pipeline).
Both sources explicitly call it a 'магистральный газопровод' (trunk/main = transmission-grade gas pipeline).

uzreport.news dated 2002-01-16 and uz2002.ru dated 2002-04-05 both describe an in-progress ITERA-financed Gazli-Kagan build targeted for completion 'к середине 2002 года' (mid-2002) -- two independent outlets, same construction year.

Sputnik explicitly states the third line opened in 2006, distinguishing it from lines 1-2 (1973-1983). Single directly-accessible independent source; the sheet's own existing Length ref (ngm.uz) likely corroborates but was unreachable today (503 + Wayback outage) so I count only Sputnik here -- medium tier.
Both sources describe the pipeline originating at the Gazli field/town, linking it to the Ustyurt and Bukhara-Khiva gas regions -- Gazli is the well-known supergiant field the corridor is named for.
Both sources confirm the pipeline runs Gazli to Kagan, both towns in Bukhara region, Uzbekistan.

Both sources give the total project cost as exactly $30 million USD ('общей стоимостью 30 млн долларов США'), financed via an ITERA credit plus Uzbekneftegaz's own funds under a government guarantee. Note this likely covers only the 2002 construction phase, not any 2005-2006 follow-on work -- flagged in validity notes, not a reason to withhold the fill since it matches the sheet's own figure exactly.

See the spec concern in validity[]: the only sourced 35 mmcm/day figure (Sputnik 2021) is the CORRIDOR-WIDE combined throughput of lines I+II+III, not segment III's own capacity, and the identical value is duplicated on sibling row P2290 (segments I+II). Citing that source here would misrepresent it as segment-specific confirmation. Leaving unresolved rather than fabricating a segment split or citing a source that doesn't actually support the per-segment claim.

The only source giving a diameter for this specific segment (1020mm, via the km 0-10/78-116 sections) traces to ngm.uz, which was unreachable today (HTTP 503, three attempts; Wayback capture also unreachable due to a web.archive.org outage). 1020mm is plausible (matches sibling P3983/segment IV and the corridor's general 720->1020mm upgrade pattern noted in search results) but I could not independently verify it from an accessible source, so leaving unresolved rather than citing a page I could not actually read.

Uztransgaz is Uzbekistan's state gas-transmission monopoly and a plausible owner, but no source I found names Uztransgaz specifically in connection with the Gazli-Kagan pipeline. The candidate utg.uz investment-program press release (from wiki_citations) is a confirmed 404 (not usable). The utg.uz shareholder page (www.utg.uz/ru/invest/aktsii-i-dividendy/) describes who owns UZTRANSGAZ THE COMPANY (Ministry of Economy and Finance 51.7%, Uzbekneftegaz 46.78%), not Uztransgaz's ownership of this pipeline asset -- citing it would misrepresent what it supports. Leaving unresolved rather than force a plausible-but-unsourced attribution.

status_reviews.researcher_notes: Searched Russian-language sources for any newer status change (decommissioning, damage, capacity change) beyond 2021. Found none. Sputnik (2021-11-29) confirms segment III (opened 2006) was one of three actively operating lines carrying a combined 35 mmcm/day at the time the 4th line was being added alongside it -- i.e. still in active service, not being replaced or retired. No evidence of any outage or status change found in 2022-2026 reporting on the corridor (the 2022 TAFSILAR piece concerns the 4th line's continued construction, not segment III). Dormancy rules do not apply (this is an operating row with recent positive evidence, not a stalled proposed/shelved project). Confirm as operating.

summary: P3984 (Gazli-Kagan Segment III) confirmed real and correctly classified via 3 independent 2002/2021 Russian sources, distinct from siblings P2290 (I+II) and P3983 (IV); 9 fields filled with verified refs (Status, Fuel, PipelineType, Construction, Start, FuelSource, Location, SegmentCost). One spec concern flagged (not fixed): Capacity=35.00 is likely the corridor-wide combined throughput of lines I+II+III misattributed as this segment's own figure, and is duplicated identically on P2290 -- needs Update-leg resolution, no source gives segment III's individual capacity. Length's existing ref (ngm.uz) could not be re-verified today (503 + Wayback outage, a network condition not a deletion) -- caveat only, ref kept. Diameter and Owner left UNRESOLVED: no independently-accessible source supports them (Diameter's only lead is the same unreachable ngm.uz page; Owner has no pipeline-specific naming, only a plausible generic attribution).
